title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nasdaq jumped 2.3% (best session since early August) and S&P 500 +1.5% to 7,764.70 as AI/chip stocks led a broad rally; Dow added 366 points (+0.7%) to 52,048.83.
Markets: Oil extended its slide - Brent fell 3.5% to just above $100/bbl, a 4th straight decline (longest since June), on hopes for Iran diplomacy at this week's UN General Assembly.
Markets: Bitcoin topped $86,000 for the first time since January, lifting Coinbase (+3.5%) and Circle (+3%) even after last week's crypto-stock selloff when the Clarity Act stalled in Congress.

Companies: Warner Bros. Discovery jumped ~11% (Paramount -3%) after Paramount settled a 12-state antitrust suit, clearing the way for its $81B WBD merger; terms include $300M/year in added film investment and a 5-year pledge to keep California studio lots.
Companies: Meta surged 11% on optimism around its new AI agent 'Muse,' with one analyst projecting $28B+ in added revenue by 2030; chipmakers and Intel rallied alongside the broader AI trade.
Macro/Policy: The Fed's Sept. 16 rate hike to 3.75%-4.00% (first since 2023) remains the backdrop, with most FOMC members open to another hike later this year; Richmond Fed's Barkin speaks today.
Macro/Policy: UN General Assembly opens today in NYC - markets watching for a possible Trump-Pezeshkian (Iran) meeting; AutoZone and KB Home report earnings.
